title: Correlation search between preoperative NOAC / DAPT pause and intraoperative or postoperative bleeding in cardiac surgery using specific coagulation diagnostics
summary: Many cardiac surgery patients already take preoperative blood thinners (new oral anticoagulants [NOAC] and/or dual antiplatelet agents [DAPT]) to prevent blood clots in the blood vessels. Some patients, after a timely break from blood thinners before surgery, may still develop bleeding during and after surgery. With the help of routine non-specific coagulation diagnostics, it is not possible to reliably determine the risk of bleeding. In our work, we want to carry out specific coagulation diagnostics for preoperatively taken blood thinners (NOAC and/or DAPT) in order to evaluate the optimal pause time before heart surgery for each drug and which other factors cause intraoperative and postoperative bleeding.

interventions.name:
NOAC-group
Measurement of DAPT/NOAC (residual) effect using additional samples (in addition to the laboratory routine) pre- (on the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th day DAPT/NOAC break) and postoperatively (on the 1st, 3rd and 5th day) in ClotPro or TEG6S and Multiplate

DAPT-group
Measurement of DAPT/NOAC (residual) effect using additional samples (in addition to the laboratory routine) pre- (on the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th day DAPT/NOAC break) and postoperatively (on the 1st, 3rd and 5th day) in ClotPro or TEG6S and Multiplate

control group
Measurement of DAPT/NOAC (residual) effect using additional samples (in addition to the laboratory routine) pre- (on the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th day DAPT/NOAC break) and postoperatively (on the 1st, 3rd and 5th day) in ClotPro or TEG6S and Multiplate

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients for planned heart surgery (e.g. coronary bypass surgery or valve surgery) with preoperative anticoagulation (therapy with apixaban / rivaroxaban / edoxaban or ticagrelor / clopidogrel / prasugrel with / without ASA with / without bridging LMWH / unfractionated heparin)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Rejection of the study
2. Patients with caregiver
